pr_title: core: Avoid race when starting dbus services
pr_body:
In high load scenarios it is possible for services to be started
before the NameOwnerChanged signal is properly installed. Revert back
to the synchronous version to avoid this occurring.

Fixes: #12956
pr_comments: hmm, i think it would be nicer to check right after we installed the match whether the name is already taken. In particular as the dbus folks want to establish a concept where names can be taken before a service is set up already (socket activation style).

> hmm, i think it would be nicer to check right after we installed the match whether the name is already taken. In particular as the dbus folks want to establish a concept where names can be taken before a service is set up already (socket activation style).

I put together a quick attempt, I think it looks weird and iffy, I seemingly need to duplicate at least the service name into Unit from Service. At this point I am a bit out of my water being my first change to the systemd code I am not sure I am up to the task of going on what feels like a much larger refactoring.

Also looking at the code I would expect there to be some check if we actually need to call GetNameOwner (i.e. has the service already started), this would either need a new callback back into the service-code or some manner of "is_already_executing" flag, possibly such exists already but a quick glance didn't give me any insight. Again, refactoring that is somewhat out of my league currently.

Not sure why install_watch is implemented at the unit level, at least https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/1782e89c9de1d98bece95bf0ab65b97aaf84f386/src/core/dbus.c#L753 assumes, hard, that all watch_bus units are of type Service. Maybe the code should just move wholesale into the service class where the name is already available?
Hmm, I think I would prefer if we keep this generic, I have some ideas where I want to reuse that for other unit types later on.

issue_context.title: NameOwnerChanged events can be lost when starting a service
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
> v239, v241

**Used distribution**
 > yocto w/ internal extra layers

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
 > Service activated over dbus is properly determined to have started

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
 > Timeout, followed by killing the service, despite the service having started properly

75152a4d6aedbfd3ee8b2d5782b9edf27407622a changed the NameOwnerChanged event to be installed asynchronously.

Since v239 we have observed occasional failure of one of our services to start, almost exclusively in specific test scenarios which causes additional load on the system during bootup.

An apparently unrelated change caused this to be near 100% reproducible on one of our (least powerful) systems. After debugging we have observed that it takes ~5 seconds from calling `add_match_async` until the `install_callback` gets called, and between then the service has been started and the NameOwnerChanged event already fired off.

Reverting back to `sd_bus_add_match` causes all failures to disappear.
